system:
You are the Issuing authority reviewer, standing in for the national emergency authority that issues alerts (who, where, when). You check that this sender may issue this alert, for this area, now: the sender is in the issuer register, the target area is the one requested for this event, the status fits the context (a drill stays a drill), it does not overreach an active alert from a higher authority, and a correction points to the alert it corrects.
You see only the issuer register, active and earlier alerts, the requested area and the alert's status, type, sender and area. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

For every objection also fill `uae_basis`: if one of the UAE clauses shown (ids starting with ITU-UAE:, TDRA-,
UAE-, DXB-) speaks to this issue, set status "cites_uae" with its id and a word-for-word quote; otherwise set
status "none_applies" with empty ref and quote. Say "none_applies" honestly: it tells the regulator where UAE
texts are silent.

[ITU-UAE:01_AI_Strategy_and_Governance/API_First_Guideline#0112] API First Guideline (p.45):
UAE Government API First Guidlines ⁞ 5.1.2⁝ GraphQL APIs GraphQL is a language for querying databases from client-side applications. It provides a set of tools that operated over a single endpoint using HTTP. On the backend, GraphQL specifies to the API how to present the data to the client. GraphQL redefines developers’ work with APIs offering more flexibility and speed to market; it improves client-server interactions by enabling the former to make precise data requests and obtain no more and no less, but exactly what they need. GraphQL offer Strongly Typed Scheme for API Queries. It ensures there is no Over-Fetching on Under-Fetching of data saving time and bandwidth. Unlike REST it requires no versioning and it elegantly handles mutations, filtering, sorting and pagination etc. It transforms the shape of the response using the GraphQL execution library to match the shape of the query

[ITU-UAE:03_Digital_Government_and_Telecom/3.4_TDRA_Spectrum_Management_White_Paper_2023#0020] 3.4 TDRA Spectrum Management White Paper 2023 (p.8):
4.1. Current Approach to Authorizing Spectrum Use TDRA’s current spectrum management tool dates from 2008 (which itself is an update of the original 2005 system). It has been subject to many updates since then. Key aspects of the original specification and subsequent development were minimal wait times for applicants and good visibility for management of the status of applications. TDRA, and the UAE government generally, places great emphasis on customer experience. As such, its systems and processes are designed to make authorisation applications as straightforward for stakeholders as possible. The TDRA provides an authorisation portal on its web site for users to apply for spectrum use as demand dictates (noting that some spectrum usage is also authorised through general authorisations or exemptions). It is also possible to modify, renew and cancel authorisations via the TDRA web site and all spectrum authorisations are now electronic. The UAE telecommunications sector is characterised as a duopoly with two main licensees: e& by Etisalat and du. There are also sector specific licensees which hold licences for specific services. To provide public telecommunications services within the UAE, applicants need to obtain a telecommunications licence.

data.summary: The sender is registered at level 1 with all areas and categories, and no higher-authority alert is active. The status and context fit: a real event is sent as Actual and the msgType is Alert with no references needed. The alert targets 'All of the UAE' (UAE-ALL), but the area requested and drawn for event uae-dust-2026-03-04 is only the Abu Dhabi coastal and inland demo zone (AUH-COAST-INLAND). That is over-broad targeting and the drafter can fix it.

objections.issue: The alert area is wider than the area requested for this event. The request is the Abu Dhabi coastal and inland zone, but the alert targets all of the UAE, so people outside the requested area would receive it.
objections.fix: Set areaDesc to 'Coastal and inland areas, Abu Dhabi (demo zone)' and codes to DEMO-ZONE / AUH-COAST-INLAND, matching the requested area. If a nationwide alert is really intended, a person at the issuing authority must decide that and redraw the area for the event.
